claims.text: A machine-learning-driven, high-throughput composition-screening approach can identify new refractory high-entropy alloys.
ML-optimized RHEAs will have higher yield strength than conventionally designed RHEAs.
ML-optimized RHEAs will have greater tensile ductility than conventionally designed RHEAs.
ML-optimized RHEAs will have lower density than conventionally designed RHEAs.
The initial material can be a polycrystalline, near-equiatomic Nb-Ti-V-Zr RHEA produced by standard melting and casting.
An integrated high-throughput computational strategy can rapidly explore a large multi-principal-element composition space.
Machine-learning models can predict mechanical properties and density directly from elemental compositions.
Adding newly tested data iteratively will refine the model's predictive accuracy.
Candidate alloys should be evaluated at room and elevated temperatures while tracking density, yield strength, and tensile ductility.
The optimized alloys will possess a body-centered-cubic matrix.
The optimized alloys may contain precipitation-strengthening phases selected through multivariate composition predictions.
Machine learning captures complex synergistic effects among multiple principal elements.
Composition guidance from machine learning can enhance solid-solution strengthening.
Composition guidance from machine learning can enhance precipitation strengthening while maintaining low density.
Existing RHEA baselines for the target properties were designed using conventional CALPHAD or heuristic methods.
ML prediction accuracy and generality may degrade when the training data inadequately represent higher-order chemical interactions or off-equiatomic compositions.
Proof-of-concept results for the proposed ML-based RHEA design strategy exist.
Model refinement and expansion of training data are needed before the strategy can be generalized to all RHEA systems.
The hypothesis can be tested by synthesizing ML-selected candidates and conventionally designed controls and measuring their density, tensile properties, and phases.
The hypothesis is falsified if the ML-selected alloys do not exceed both the yield strength and ductility of the controls while also maintaining lower relative density.
